about: LDP and LD3 against their authors' code on the models their papers plant, with global PC read at the pair beside them; the release summary's LDP and LD3 entries are built from it
build: Andrey pre-release build of 16 November 2026 (the 0.18.0 release branch with ld3's direct criterion given every parent found and ldp's Z5 criterion read with the instruments independent of every confounder found, as merged in this change)
hardware: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; every arm of a cell ran in one job on shared nodes, so the times are indicative
verdict_rule: per cell (20 datasets, seeds 0-19, one treatment-outcome pair each): per dataset D = Andrey's error minus the authors' code's on the same data; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly above 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly below, a tie otherwise (a tie too when the two errors are equal on every dataset). A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on a measure is rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree. The floor: per dataset, the error minus the floor's (the empty adjustment set for valid_set_loss, parents_error, and effect_error; for LD3's direct_error the better constant answer over the 40 datasets of a size with and without the direct effect); it applies where the authors' code's interval lies wholly below 0, and a row then passes when Andrey's does too
error_metric: valid_set_loss: 1 when LDP returns no adjustment set or a set that is not a valid adjustment set for the pair in the true DAG (hidden variables included), else 0; effect_error: the mean absolute error of the effect estimated with the returned set on a fresh sample, in standard deviations (a set-free answer has none); parents_error: 1 unless LD3's set is the outcome's true parents other than the treatment; direct_error: 1 when the answer's nonzero for the direct effect is not the truth's (an edge from the treatment to the outcome)
fit_protocol: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, no warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored; no fit failed or timed out. The same level on both arms: Fisher's z at 0.01 on the Gaussian cells (the papers' level) and Pearson's chi-square at 0.001 on MILDEW (LDP's Figure 6), where Andrey refers the statistic to its mean under a shuffle (its default degrees of freedom) and the authors' code to (r - 1)(c - 1) per configuration over the values present
seeds_note: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19, and 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39
cells_note: ldp@<rows>[,effect=0]: LDP's 10-variable partition graph (its Figure 3), linear Gaussian, every coefficient 1 and the treatment's effect 2.75 (0 without the arc); ldp@5000,latent=True,hide=<nodes>: its 18-variable graph (Figure E.5), linear Gaussian, the named nodes hidden; mildew@<rows>: the MILDEW network's tables, treatment mikro_1, outcome meldug_2, dm_1 and foto_1 hidden; ld3-dag@<rows>[,effect=0][,hide=<node>]: LD3's 18-variable graph (its Figure D.1 with the authors' code's Z7 and Z8), linear Gaussian, direct effect 1.25 (0 without the arc), other coefficients uniform on [0.75, 1.1]; ld3-er@5000,nodes=<d>: random graphs with 1.5 d arcs whose outcome is the leaf with the most parents, a random parent the treatment; sangiovese@<rows>: the fitted SANGIOVESE network, treatment pH, outcome GrapeW (a sink); the columns in an order drawn from the seed
pareto_note: pareto: Andrey's method against global PC read at the pair (andrey.pc.adjustment) with the same test and level, effect error against seconds per fit; PC is better on both only when its paired interval lies wholly below Andrey's error and its median seconds are lower; an abstention has no effect error, so cells where PC abstains on most datasets pair fewer than 10
